 Advertisement Here's how many people in Maine have voted by mail ahead of the 2026 midterm election
 The Hearst Get the Facts Data Team is tracking early ballots ahead of Election Day, Nov. 3.
 Advertisement Updated: 9:49 PM EDT Oct 29, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Russ Reed Here's how many people in Maine have voted by mail ahead of the 2026 midterm election
 The Hearst Get the Facts Data Team is tracking early ballots ahead of Election Day, Nov. 3.
 Updated: 9:49 PM EDT Oct 29, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Russ Reed AUGUSTA, Maine — The Hearst Get the Facts Data Team is tracking early and mail-in ballots that have been cast ahead of the 2026 midterm election.
 The data comes from the University of Florida Election Lab , which has tracked early voting data since 2008 and also aggregates turnout and results data. Early voting counts are compiled directly from state and regional sources.
 Advertisement As of 9:45 p.m. Thursday, more than 273,900 mail-in ballots have been returned in Maine. The UF Election Lab does not have data from Maine when it comes to early in-person voting. 
 Use the map above to see how many early votes have been cast in each state, including mail-in ballots accepted and early votes. The data does not show election results, just the number of votes that have been cast.
 Voters in Maine, 30 other states and Washington, D.C., can register under a party affiliation.
 According to the data, 47.4% of the mail-in ballots that have been received in Maine have been cast by registered Democrats, while 22.6% have been cast by Republicans. The remaining 29.9% of mail-in ballots were cast by unenrolled voters.
 The Maine Secretary of State's Office said that as of Thursday, it had issued 312,874 absentee ballots, including ballots that were given to people who vote early in person. The office said 275,563 absentee ballots had been returned and accepted. The office said 674 absentee ballots had been returned and rejected. The most common reason for a ballot to be rejected is because the voter did not sign the envelope.
 Information about early voting in Maine
 In the lead-up to Election Day, which is Nov. 3, Maine election officials encouraged voters to make their absentee ballot request early in order to allow enough time for the ballot to be mailed to them. Voters who were planning to use the U.S. mail to receive their absentee ballot should have made the request no later than 15 days prior to Election Day, which was Monday, Oct. 19, for this election.
 Maine voters can also request an absentee ballot online until 5 p.m. on the third business day prior to the election, which this year is Thursday, Oct. 29.
 Absentee ballots can be delivered via mail or dropped off either in person or via absentee ballot drop box at a municipal clerk's office.
 Voters who wish to send their absentee ballots back by U.S. mail are advised to send their ballot no later than seven days before Election Day, which is Tuesday, Oct. 27, for the Nov. 3 election. The Secretary of State's Office said the U.S. Postal Service has assured that all absentee ballots that are put in the mail at least a week before Election Day are guaranteed to be delivered in time to be cast and counted in the election.
 In order to be counted, absentee ballots must be received by a municipal clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3.
 Maine has an absentee ballot tracking system that shows voters the date their application was accepted by their municipal clerk, the date their clerk mailed out their absentee ballot and the date the clerk received the ballot. Click here to check the status of your absentee ballot .
 Since Oct. 5 , Maine voters have been able to vote early in person. The deadline for absentee voting in the presence of a municipal clerk is 5 p.m. on the Thursday before the election, which is Oct. 29 for the general election — unless special circumstances exist.
 More information about this election is available in our Maine voter guide .
